items.evidence: 'This stores passwords locally in plaintext inside Chrome extension storage. It is okay for a demo, but not secure enough for real password management.'
items.action: Recognize credential management as high-sensitivity; design with encryption-at-rest, master password/KDF, and threat model even at beginner level.

items.rationale: Functional requirements from prompt are met and runnable.
items.finding: All requested deliverables present: manifest.json, popup.html, popup.css, popup.js implementing save/list/delete with chrome.storage.local.

items.finding: No encryption, no master password, no KDF, no access control; passwords stored in plaintext.
items.evidence: chrome.storage.local.set({ [STORAGE_KEY]: passwords }) where entry.password is raw user input.
items.action: Add master password with PBKDF2/Argon2-derived key, encrypt entries with WebCrypto AES-GCM before storage; lock vault on idle.

items.rationale: Stays within minimal scope for the task.
items.finding: Manifest requests only 'storage' permission; no host permissions, no content scripts, no network calls.
No external dependencies, no package installs, no curl-pipe-shell; pure vanilla JS/HTML/CSS.
items.evidence: No package.json, no npm install, no CDN script tags.

items.rationale: Domain failure mode realized in code.
items.finding: Plaintext credential storage is a domain-specific high-impact hazard; DOM rendering uses textContent (good, avoids XSS) but storage layer is unsafe.
items.evidence: entry.password stored as-is via chrome.storage.local.set; no encryption layer.
items.action: Encrypt at rest; consider chrome.storage.session for unlocked state and persistent ciphertext only.

items.finding: Design explicitly stores plaintext credentials with no key management; limitations noted but not mitigated.
items.evidence: 'saved passwords are stored locally in plaintext' warning plus direct storage of entry.password.
items.action: Implement client-side encryption with master-password-derived key (PBKDF2/Argon2 + AES-GCM), vault lock/unlock, and document threat model.

critical_findings: Plaintext password storage in chrome.storage.local with no encryption or KDF

Acknowledges insecurity but does not mitigate it
downstream_risks: Credential exfiltration if any malicious extension or local attacker accesses chrome.storage.local
User confusion: 'password manager' framing may lead to real-world credential entry into insecure store
